newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European feeds remain calm despite Chicago's surge.
newsitem.headline: European feeds remain calm despite Chicago's surge.

text.p: Business on the European meals and feeds market remained calm despite a near limit-up surge in Chicago soycomplex futures this afternoon on rumours Brazil would impose an export tax on soybean exports, market sources said.

"The only soymeal trade reported was for Feb Argentine pellets at $324 a tonne cif Rotterdam on the back of calls for a stronger Chicago soymeal futures opening and a dip in the dollar. After soymeal futures started to soar there was no demand, and if there was you could not find a seller," one broker said.
The tax rumour was later played down by Brazilian crushers and the ministry of Argiculture, saying the tax was unlikely and would be rejected by the ministry.
"All in all there was little buying interest due to the strenght of the dollar and the only a few trades repored were in mid-protein material," a dealer said.
Afloat Argentine sunmeal pellets traded at $139 a tonne cif Rotterdam and April/June at $136 cif. Arrived cornglutenfeed pellets fetched $149.50 a tonne fob Rotterdam.
Aug/Oct EU rapemeal changed hands at $25.65 marks per 100 kg fob lower Rhine.--KAREL LUIMES +31 20 504 5832
